title: orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured
intention: orient's floor AUTHORS the packet fields that are lookup rather than language — refs, domain, unknowns — and provenance for them stops being declared by the author and becomes DERIVED from whether the ceiling changed the floor's answer.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-14 over all 45 berthed orient packets, and the measurement is the reason this is a build and not a tidy-up: NOTHING IN THE CODE PRODUCES A PACKET FIELD. The floor (floor_facts) emits facts — components_mentioned, skills_mentioned, paths_found, paths_missing, roster_size — and the ceiling then writes all five authored fields by hand and STAMPS ITS OWN PROVENANCE. domain is labelled 'floor' in 18 of 45 packets and 14 of those floor-labelled values are over 200 characters of prose; refs is labelled 'floor' in 44 of 45 while the SELECTION was always the ceiling's. So skills/chart/dial.py reads orient at 0.40 floor, and that 0.40 is a self-report. THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is Akien's: he is deciding what to build next off that dial. A pass that reports itself 40% compiled when it is 0% compiled tells him the cheapest remaining work is elsewhere, and the staircase stalls on a number nobody computed. Under the ruling of the same day the stakes are larger than tidiness — the ceiling for the preamble is becoming Hex, and the whole point of a failover is that it DEPOSITS, so 'what did the floor already answer' has to be a fact before 'what did the ceiling have to add' can be one.
traces_to: Ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap — the build order is Akien's: 'starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now ... those can be completely deterministic. and ONCE THEY WORK we can start working on the other ones later.'
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A provenance the author stamps is an unmeasured claim wearing a measurement's name.
Law 4 — a rule enforced by physics, not policy. 'label the field honestly' is discipline; deriving the label removes the discretion.
Law 9 — red is the default, green is earned. 0.40 floor is a green the corpus never earned.

Akien's 2026-07-19 pre-build-packet paper, the staircase section: 'migrate a pass only when its deterministic version passes a check a hollow one couldn't.' A self-reported provenance is exactly the check a hollow version passes.

falsifier.proves_green: TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND IS WHAT MAKES THE FIRST HONEST. (1) floor_packet(request, root) authors refs (paths the floor verified plus the directories of components and skills it matched), domain (the addresses and their rung on tools->machines->devices->skills, derived from where those refs actually sit), and unknowns (what the floor could NOT ground — paths claimed in the request that do not exist, slash-verbs not in the skill roster). (2) PROVENANCE FOR THOSE THREE IS DERIVED, NOT ACCEPTED: the packet door compares the ceiling's field against the floor's proposal and writes 'floor' when it survived unchanged, 'claude' when it did not. A caller-supplied provenance for those fields is refused rather than trusted. The ceiling keeps intent and scope, which need language. THE CEILING MUST STILL EXTEND unknowns — the floor's unknowns are UNGROUNDABLE REFERENCES and the ceiling's are conceptual ('whether the proof or the inspector is the shaker'); a floor that crowds out the conceptual ones has made the packet worse while making the dial look better, which is this build's own worst failure mode.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) a packet is berthed whose provenance for refs/domain/unknowns was written by its sender rather than derived — the self-report restored; (2) the derived floor fraction goes UP while the packets get thinner, i.e. the ceiling stopped adding conceptual unknowns because the floor had already filled the field (the crowding-out failure, and the dial would read this as progress); (3) a floor-authored ref does not exist on disk, which the existing every_ref_exists_on_disk check must catch — a floor that invents is worse than a ceiling that invents, because it wears the provenance of a measurement; (4) domain becomes prose again by any route, since the whole point is that it is derived from where the refs sit; (5) the change lands in orient and the dial's reading for the other six nexi is left looking comparable when it is no longer measuring the same thing.
falsifier.horizon: Now. It is the first rung of the build order Akien named the same day, and everything after it (constrain, then survey) inherits both halves — the second half especially, because a derived provenance built once at orient is the pattern the other two are written from, and a self-report copied forward is exactly how 'a tool holds no state' reached eight charters.

chart_notes.orient: The code is at cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/orient.py: floor_facts (:82) emits the facts, AUTHORED_FIELDS (:69) names the five the ceiling writes, inspect_orient (:123) already checks ref existence and provenance coverage, validate_orient (:183) is the gate, write_packet (:208) is the berth. The instructing prose is skills/chart/SKILL.md stage 1. The reading instrument is skills/chart/dial.py. The evidence is 45 berthed orient packets under ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/.
chart_notes.constrain: IN: orient only. OUT: constrain and survey (they are the next two rungs and inherit the pattern, but Akien's order is one at a time and 'ONCE THEY WORK'); the other six nexi's dial readings; anything on hex.local; and any change to the dial's own code. Also OUT: widening AUTHORED_FIELDS or changing the packet schema's shape — the fields stay the five they are.
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails: berth a packet whose sender DECLARES provenance floor for a domain it wrote by hand, and require the door to refuse it or to overwrite the label with 'claude'. A hollow build passes by accepting the sender's dict, which is exactly today's behaviour. Second tooth: run floor_packet on a request naming a path that does not exist and require it to land in unknowns rather than in refs — a floor that invents a ref is the worst failure here, because it carries a measurement's provenance.
